```java
                    // Set up event subscription and track it
                    HomekitEventSubscription subscription = subscribeToCharacteristicEvents(characteristic);
                    if (subscription != null) {
                        eventSubscriptions.put(characteristic.getUID().toString(), subscription);

                }
```

```java
    private void handleItemCommand(ItemCommandEvent event) {
        String itemName = event.getItemName();
        Command command = event.getItemCommand();

        // Find characteristic for this item
        characteristicMap.entrySet().stream()
                .filter(entry -> itemName.equals(itemMap.get(entry.getKey())))
                .map(Map.Entry::getValue)
                .findFirst()
                .ifPresent(characteristic -> {

                                null,
                                Map.<String, Object>of(),
                                new HomekitEventMetadata(bridgeUID, null, bridgeUID, peerGroup));

                                e.getMessage());
                    }
                });

    private void handleItemState(ItemStateEvent event) {
        String itemName = event.getItemName();
        State state = event.getItemState();

        // Clean up expired exit events
        exitEvents.entrySet().removeIf(entry -> entry.getValue().isExpired());

        // Find characteristic for this item
        characteristicMap.entrySet().stream()
                .filter(entry -> itemName.equals(itemMap.get(entry.getKey())))
                .map(Map.Entry::getValue)
                .findFirst()
                .ifPresent(characteristic -> {
                    try {
                        ExitEvent exitEvent = exitEvents.get(itemName);
```

```java
// ... existing code ...
    private void handleAccessoryAdded(HomekitAccessory accessory, HomekitAccessoryServer remoteServer) {
        if (orphanEnabled) {
            // Check if this is a restoration of an orphaned accessory
            BridgeContext existingContext = bridgedAccessories.get(accessory);
            if (existingContext != null && existingContext.localAccessory.isOrphaned()) {
                if (restoreOrphanedAccessory(accessory, existingContext)) {
                    logger.info("{}Successfully restored orphaned accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID());
                    return;
                }
            }
        }

        // Continue with normal bridging process
        if (isRemoteServer(remoteServer)) {
            try {
                // Create local copy of the accessory
                HomekitAccessory localAccessory = createLocalAccessoryCopy(accessory);
                if (localAccessory == null) {
                    logger.error("{}Failed to create local copy of accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID());
                    return;
                }

                // Get available local server
                Optional<HomekitAccessoryServer> localServerOpt = Optional.ofNullable(serverRegistry.getAvailableBridgeAccessoryServer());
                if (localServerOpt.isEmpty()) {
                    logger.error("{}No available local server found for accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID());
                    return;
                }

                // Add to local server
                HomekitAccessoryServer localServer = localServerOpt.get();
                localServer.addAccessory(localAccessory);

                // Store bridge context
                BridgeContext context = new BridgeContext(localAccessory, localServer, remoteServer);
                bridgedAccessories.put(accessory, context);

                logger.info("{}Successfully bridged accessory {} from remote server to local server", LOG_PREFIX,
                        accessory.getUID());
            } catch (Exception e) {
                logger.error("{}Failed to bridge accessory {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID(), e.getMessage(), e);
            }
        }
    }

    private void handleAccessoryRemoved(HomekitAccessory accessory) {
        BridgeContext context = bridgedAccessories.get(accessory);
        if (context != null) {
            if (orphanEnabled) {
                // Mark the accessory as orphaned but keep it in the registry
                logger.info("{}Accessory {} was removed but keeping it to prevent controller deletion", LOG_PREFIX,
                        accessory.getUID());
                context.localAccessory.setOrphaned(true);

                // Update configuration to reflect orphaned state
                try {
                    Map<String, Object> accessoryConfig = new HashMap<>();
                    accessoryConfig.put("orphaned", true);
                    configManager.updateConfiguration((UID) accessory.getUID(),
                            HomekitConfigurationManager.ConfigurationType.ACCESSORY, accessoryConfig);
                } catch (Exception e) {
                    logger.error("{}Failed to update configuration for orphaned accessory {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX,
                            accessory.getUID(), e.getMessage(), e);
                }
            } else {
                // Completely remove the accessory and its characteristics
                try {
                    context.localServer.removeAccessory(context.localAccessory);
                    bridgedAccessories.remove(accessory);
                    logger.info("{}Successfully removed accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID());
                } catch (Exception e) {
                    logger.error("{}Failed to remove accessory {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID(), e.getMessage(),
                            e);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Restores an orphaned accessory if its remote counterpart becomes available again.
     *
     * @param remoteAccessory The remote accessory that was added
     * @param context The bridge context containing the orphaned accessory
     * @return true if the accessory was successfully restored, false otherwise
     */
    private boolean restoreOrphanedAccessory(HomekitAccessory remoteAccessory, BridgeContext context) {
        try {
            // Remove orphaned flag
            context.localAccessory.setOrphaned(false);

            // Update configuration to reflect restored state
            Map<String, Object> config = new HashMap<>();
            config.put("orphaned", false);
            configManager.updateConfiguration((UID) remoteAccessory.getUID(),
                    HomekitConfigurationManager.ConfigurationType.ACCESSORY, config);

            // Re-subscribe to characteristic events
            context.localAccessory.getServices().forEach(service -> {
                service.getCharacteristics().forEach(characteristic -> {
                    HomekitEventSubscription subscription = subscribeToCharacteristicEvents(characteristic);
                    if (subscription != null) {
                        eventSubscriptions.put(characteristic.getUID().toString(), subscription);
                    }
                });
            });

            logger.info("{}Successfully restored orphaned accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, remoteAccessory.getUID());
            return true;
        } catch (Exception e) {
            logger.error("{}Failed to restore orphaned accessory {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX, remoteAccessory.getUID(),
                    e.getMessage(), e);
            return false;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Checks if an accessory is orphaned.
     *
     * @param accessory The {@link HomekitAccessory} to check
     * @return true if the accessory is orphaned, false otherwise
     */
    public boolean isOrphaned(HomekitAccessory accessory) {
        BridgeContext ctx = bridgedAccessories.get(accessory);
        return ctx != null && ctx.localAccessory.isOrphaned();
    }

     * Creates a local copy of a remote accessory.

    private HomekitAccessory createLocalAccessoryCopy(HomekitAccessory remoteAccessory) {
        try {
            // Create new accessory of the same type
            HomekitAccessory localAccessory = accessoryFactory.createAccessory(remoteAccessory.getType());
            if (localAccessory == null) {
                return null;
            }

            // Copy metadata and configuration
            remoteAccessory.getServices().forEach(remoteService -> {
                Optional<HomekitService> localService = localAccessory.getService(remoteService.getType());
                if (localService.isPresent()) {
                    remoteService.getCharacteristics().forEach(remoteChar -> {
                        localService.get().getCharacteristics().stream()
                                .filter(c -> c.getTag().equals(remoteChar.getTag()))
                                .findFirst()
                                .ifPresent(localChar -> {
                                    try {
                                        localChar.setValue(remoteChar.getValue());
                                    } catch (Exception e) {
                                        logger.warn("{}Failed to copy characteristic value: {}", LOG_PREFIX,
                                                e.getMessage());
                                    }
                                });
                    });
                }
            });

            return localAccessory;
        } catch (Exception e) {
            logger.error("{}Failed to create local accessory copy: {}", LOG_PREFIX, e.getMessage(), e);
            return null;
        }
    }
```

   - The HomeKit controller maintains its configuration based on the accessory's presence
   - As long as the accessory remains registered with the server, the HomeKit controller's configuration is preserved
   - The accessory can still respond to HomeKit requests even if its linked Items/Things are offline

```java
    /**
     * Handles the addition of a new accessory.
     *
     * This method processes accessory addition events, creating local copies and
     * setting up bridging when appropriate.
     *
     * @param accessory The {@link HomekitAccessory} that was added
     * @param remoteServer The {@link HomekitAccessoryServer} the accessory was added to
     * @since 1.0.0
     */
    public void handleAccessoryAdded(HomekitAccessory accessory, HomekitAccessoryServer remoteServer) {
        // Continue with normal bridging process
        if (isRemoteServer(remoteServer)) {
            try {
                // Create local copy of the accessory
                HomekitAccessory localAccessory = createLocalAccessoryCopy(accessory);
                if (localAccessory == null) {
                    logger.error("{}Failed to create local copy of accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID());
                    return;
                }

                // Get available local server
                Optional<HomekitAccessoryServer> localServerOpt = Optional.ofNullable(serverRegistry.getAvailableBridgeAccessoryServer());
                if (localServerOpt.isEmpty()) {
                    logger.error("{}No available local server found for accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID());
                    return;
                }

                // Add to local server
                HomekitAccessoryServer localServer = localServerOpt.get();
                localServer.addAccessory(localAccessory);

                // Store bridge context
                BridgeContext context = new BridgeContext(localAccessory, localServer, remoteServer);
                bridgedAccessories.put(accessory, context);

                logger.info("{}Successfully bridged accessory {} from remote server to local server", LOG_PREFIX,
                        accessory.getUID());
            } catch (Exception e) {
                logger.error("{}Failed to bridge accessory {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID(), e.getMessage(), e);
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Handles the removal of an accessory.
     *
     * This method processes accessory removal events, cleaning up bridging resources
     * and handling any necessary state updates.
     *
     * @param accessory The {@link HomekitAccessory} that was removed
     * @since 1.0.0
     */
    public void handleAccessoryRemoved(HomekitAccessory accessory) {
        BridgeContext context = bridgedAccessories.get(accessory);
        if (context != null) {
            // Completely remove the accessory and its characteristics
            try {
                context.localServer.removeAccessory(context.localAccessory);
                bridgedAccessories.remove(accessory);
                logger.info("{}Successfully removed accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID());
            } catch (Exception e) {
                logger.error("{}Failed to remove accessory {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX, accessory.getUID(), e.getMessage(),
                        e);
            }
        }
    }

    private void handleAccessoryAdded(HomekitAccessoryServerEvent event) {
        if (event.getAccessory() == null) {
            return;
        }

        HomekitAccessory accessory = event.getAccessory().orElse(null);
        if (bridgedAccessories.containsKey(accessory)) {
            return;
        }

        // Add the accessory to our registry
        bridgedAccessories.put(accessory, new BridgeContext(accessory, event.getServer().orElse(null), null));

        // Subscribe to characteristic events
        accessory.getServices().forEach(service -> {
            service.getCharacteristics().forEach(characteristic -> {
                if (characteristic instanceof AbstractHomekitCharacteristic) {
                    AbstractHomekitCharacteristic<?> abstractCharacteristic = (AbstractHomekitCharacteristic<?>) characteristic;
                    HomekitCharacteristicUIDImpl characteristicUID = (HomekitCharacteristicUIDImpl) abstractCharacteristic.getUID();
                    // TODO: CHARACTERISTIC_CHANGED event type and related subscription logic
                }
            });
        });

        logger.info("{}Added accessory {} to bridge", LOG_ACCESSORY, accessory.getUID());
    }

    private void handleAccessoryRemoved(HomekitAccessoryServerEvent event) {
        if (event.getAccessory() == null) {
            return;
        }

        HomekitAccessory accessory = event.getAccessory().orElse(null);
        BridgeContext context = bridgedAccessories.get(accessory);
        if (context == null) {
            return;
        }

        // Remove the accessory from our registry
        bridgedAccessories.remove(accessory);
        logger.info("{}Removed accessory {} from bridge", LOG_ACCESSORY, accessory.getUID());
    }
```

```java
    private void loadConfiguration() {
        // Load accessory configuration from YAML
        Optional<Map<String, Object>> config = configManager.getConfiguration(null,
                HomekitConfigurationManager.ConfigurationType.ACCESSORY);
        if (config.isEmpty()) {
            logger.warn("{}No accessory configuration found", LOG_PREFIX);
            return;
        }

        // Process each accessory in the configuration
        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
        Map<String, Object> accessories = (Map<String, Object>) config.get().get("accessories");
        if (accessories != null) {
            // Create or update configured accessories
            accessories.forEach((uid, accessoryConfig) -> {
                if (accessoryMap.containsKey(uid)) {
                    updateAccessory(uid, (Map<String, Object>) accessoryConfig);
                } else {
                    createAccessory(uid, (Map<String, Object>) accessoryConfig);
                }
            });
        } else {
            // If no accessories in config, remove all existing ones
            accessoryMap.keySet().forEach(this::removeAccessory);
        }
    }
```

```java
    private void createAccessory(String uid, Map<String, Object> accessoryConfig) {
        try {
            // Get accessory type
            String type = (String) accessoryConfig.get("type");
            if (type == null) {
                logger.error("{}No type specified for accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, uid);
                return;
            }

            // Create accessory, fall back to generic if type not supported
            HomekitAccessory accessory = accessoryFactory.createAccessory(type);
            if (accessory == null) {
                logger.warn("{}Type {} not supported, falling back to generic type for accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, type, uid);
                accessory = accessoryFactory.createAccessory("generic");
                if (accessory == null) {
                    logger.error("{}Failed to create generic accessory for {}", LOG_PREFIX, uid);
                    return;
                }
            }

            // Apply metadata
            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
            Map<String, Object> metadata = (Map<String, Object>) accessoryConfig.get("metadata");
            if (metadata != null) {
                applyMetadata(accessory, metadata);
            }

            // Process services
            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
            Map<String, Object> services = (Map<String, Object>) accessoryConfig.get("services");
            if (services != null) {
                processServices(accessory, services);
            }

            // Register accessory
```

```java
    private void createAccessory(String uid, Map<String, Object> accessoryConfig) {
        try {
            // Get accessory type
            String type = (String) accessoryConfig.get("type");
            if (type == null) {
                logger.error("{}No type specified for accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, uid);
                return;
            }

            // Check if type is supported, fall back to generic if not
            if (!accessoryFactory.supportsAccessoryType(type)) {
                logger.warn("{}Type {} not supported, falling back to generic type for accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, type, uid);
                type = "generic";
                if (!accessoryFactory.supportsAccessoryType(type)) {
                    logger.error("{}Generic type not supported by factory for accessory {}", LOG_PREFIX, uid);
                    return;
                }
            }

            // Create accessory
            HomekitAccessory accessory = accessoryFactory.createAccessory(type);
            if (accessory == null) {
                logger.error("{}Failed to create accessory of type {} for {}", LOG_PREFIX, type, uid);
                return;
            }

            // Apply metadata
            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
            Map<String, Object> metadata = (Map<String, Object>) accessoryConfig.get("metadata");
            if (metadata != null) {
                applyMetadata(accessory, metadata);
            }

            // Process services
            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
            Map<String, Object> services = (Map<String, Object>) accessoryConfig.get("services");
            if (services != null) {
                processServices(accessory, services);

            // Register accessory

                accessoryMap.put(uid, accessory);
                logger.info("{}Successfully created accessory {} of type {}", LOG_PREFIX, uid,
```

```java
    private void applyCharacteristicConfig(HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic, Map<String, Object> config) {
        // Handle item/channel mapping
        String itemName = (String) config.get("item");
        String channelId = (String) config.get("channel");
        if (itemName != null) {
            try {
                ItemUID itemUID = new ItemUID(itemName);
                itemMap.put(characteristic.getUID().toString(), itemUID.toString());
            } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
                logger.warn("{}Invalid item UID format {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX, itemName, e.getMessage());
            }
        }
        if (channelId != null) {
            channelMap.put(characteristic.getUID().toString(), new ChannelUID(channelId));
        }

        // Apply other configuration (optional setters)
        if (characteristic instanceof AbstractHomekitCharacteristic<?> abstractCharacteristic) {
            if (config.containsKey("minValue")) {
                Object value = config.get("minValue");
                try {
                    var m = abstractCharacteristic.getClass().getMethod("withMinValue", double.class);
                    if (value instanceof Number) {
                        m.invoke(abstractCharacteristic, ((Number) value).doubleValue());
                    }
                } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            }
            if (config.containsKey("maxValue")) {
                Object value = config.get("maxValue");
                try {
                    var m = abstractCharacteristic.getClass().getMethod("withMaxValue", double.class);
                    if (value instanceof Number) {
                        m.invoke(abstractCharacteristic, ((Number) value).doubleValue());
                    }
                } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            }
            if (config.containsKey("step")) {
                Object value = config.get("step");
                try {
                    var m = abstractCharacteristic.getClass().getMethod("withStep", double.class);
                    if (value instanceof Number) {
                        m.invoke(abstractCharacteristic, ((Number) value).doubleValue());
                    }
                } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            }
            if (config.containsKey("inverted")) {
                Object value = config.get("inverted");
                try {
                    var m = abstractCharacteristic.getClass().getMethod("withInverted", Boolean.class);
                    if (value instanceof Boolean) {
                        m.invoke(abstractCharacteristic, value);
                    }
                } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            }
        }
    }
```

```java
    private void processCharacteristics(HomekitService service, Map<String, Object> characteristics) {
        characteristics.forEach((type, config) -> {
            try {
                HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic = characteristicFactory.createCharacteristic(type, service);
                if (characteristic != null) {
                    // Apply characteristic configuration
                    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
                    Map<String, Object> charConfig = (Map<String, Object>) config;
                    applyCharacteristicConfig(characteristic, charConfig);

                    // Add to service
                    service.addCharacteristic(characteristic);
                    characteristicMap.put(characteristic.getUID().toString(), characteristic);

                    // Set up event subscription and track it
                    HomekitEventSubscription subscription = subscribeToCharacteristicEvents(characteristic);
                    if (subscription != null) {
                        eventSubscriptions.add(subscription);
                    }
                }
            } catch (Exception e) {
                logger.error("{}Failed to create characteristic {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX, type, e.getMessage());
            }
        });
    }

            if (config.containsKey("minValue")) {
                Object value = config.get("minValue");
                try {
                    var m = abstractCharacteristic.getClass().getMethod("withMinValue", double.class);
                    if (value instanceof Number) {
                        m.invoke(abstractCharacteristic, ((Number) value).doubleValue());
                    }
                } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            }
            if (config.containsKey("maxValue")) {
                Object value = config.get("maxValue");
                try {
                    var m = abstractCharacteristic.getClass().getMethod("withMaxValue", double.class);
                    if (value instanceof Number) {
                        m.invoke(abstractCharacteristic, ((Number) value).doubleValue());
                    }
                } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            }
            if (config.containsKey("step")) {
                Object value = config.get("step");
                try {
                    var m = abstractCharacteristic.getClass().getMethod("withStep", double.class);
                    if (value instanceof Number) {
                        m.invoke(abstractCharacteristic, ((Number) value).doubleValue());
                    }
                } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            }
            if (config.containsKey("inverted")) {
                Object value = config.get("inverted");
                try {
                    var m = abstractCharacteristic.getClass().getMethod("withInverted", Boolean.class);
                    if (value instanceof Boolean) {
                        m.invoke(abstractCharacteristic, value);
                    }
                } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            }
        }
    }
```

```java
    private void handleCharacteristicEvent(HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic, HomekitEvent event) {
        if (event instanceof HomekitCharacteristicChangedEvent changedEvent) {
            try {
                // Check if event is from peer group
                if (event.getMetadata().isFromPeerGroup(peerGroup)) {
                    logger.debug("{}Ignoring event from peer group: {}", LOG_PREFIX,
                            event.getMetadata().getImmediateOrigin());
                    return;
                }

                // Handle item mapping
                ItemUID itemUID = itemMap.get(characteristic.getUID().toString());
                if (itemUID != null) {
                    State newState = characteristic.toState(changedEvent.getNewValue().orElse(null));
                    if (newState != null) {
                        exitEvents.put(itemUID.toString(), new ExitEvent(newState, event.getMetadata()));
                        eventPublisher.post(ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent(itemUID.getItemName(), newState));
                    }
                }

                logger.error("{}Failed to handle characteristic event: {}", LOG_PREFIX, e.getMessage());
            }
        }

    private void handleItemCommand(ItemCommandEvent event) {
        String itemName = event.getItemName();
        Command command = event.getItemCommand();

        // Find characteristic for this item
        characteristicMap.entrySet().stream()
                .filter(entry -> {
                    ItemUID itemUID = itemMap.get(entry.getKey());
                    return itemUID != null && itemUID.getItemName().equals(itemName);
                })
                .map(Map.Entry::getValue)
                .findFirst()
                .ifPresent(characteristic -> {
                    try {

                                characteristic.toValueJson((State) command),
                                null,

                        eventManager.publishEvent(updateEvent);
                    } catch (Exception e) {
                        logger.error("{}Failed to handle command for item {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX, itemName,
                                e.getMessage());
                    }
                });
    }

    private void handleItemState(ItemStateEvent event) {
        String itemName = event.getItemName();
        State state = event.getItemState();

        // Clean up expired exit events
        exitEvents.entrySet().removeIf(entry -> entry.getValue().isExpired());

        // Find characteristic for this item
        characteristicMap.entrySet().stream()
                .filter(entry -> {
                    ItemUID itemUID = itemMap.get(entry.getKey());
                    return itemUID != null && itemUID.getItemName().equals(itemName);
                })
                .map(Map.Entry::getValue)
                .findFirst()
                .ifPresent(characteristic -> {
                    try {
                        ExitEvent exitEvent = exitEvents.get(itemName);
                        if (exitEvent != null && !exitEvent.isExpired()) {
                            if (statesEqual(exitEvent.getState(), state)) {
                                if (ENABLE_EXIT_EVENT_STATISTICS) {
                                    statisticsCollector.recordEvent(System.currentTimeMillis() - exitEvent.getTimestamp());
                                }
                                HomekitCharacteristicUpdateEvent updateEvent = new HomekitCharacteristicUpdateEvent(
                                        (UID) bridgeUID,
                                        (UID) characteristic.getUID(),
                                        characteristic,
                                        characteristic.toValueJson(exitEvent.getState()),
                                        characteristic.toValueJson(state),
                                        Map.<String, Object>of(),
                                        new HomekitEventMetadata(bridgeUID, null, bridgeUID, peerGroup));
                                eventManager.publishEvent(updateEvent);
                                exitEvents.remove(itemName);
                            }
                        } else {
                            HomekitCharacteristicUpdateEvent updateEvent = new HomekitCharacteristicUpdateEvent(
                                    (UID) bridgeUID,
                                    (UID) characteristic.getUID(),
                                    characteristic,
                                    characteristic.toValueJson(state),
                                    null,
                                    Map.<String, Object>of(),
                                    new HomekitEventMetadata(bridgeUID, null, bridgeUID, peerGroup));
                            eventManager.publishEvent(updateEvent);
                        }
                    } catch (Exception e) {
                        logger.error("{}Failed to handle state for item {}: {}", LOG_PREFIX, itemName, e.getMessage());
                    }
                });
    }
```

```java
                logger.warn("{}Received null command for item {}", LOG_PREFIX, event.getItemName());
                return;
            }

            // Create an exit event for this command
            exitEvents.put(event.getItemName(), new ExitEvent(command, System.currentTimeMillis() + EXIT_EVENT_TIMEOUT));

                    jsonValue,
```

```java
// ... existing code ...

private void handleCharacteristicEvent(HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic, HomekitEvent event) {
    if (event instanceof HomekitCharacteristicChangedEvent changedEvent) {
        try {
            // Check if event is from peer group
            if (event.getMetadata().isFromPeerGroup(peerGroup)) {
                logger.debug("{}Ignoring event from peer group: {}", LOG_PREFIX,
                        event.getMetadata().getImmediateOrigin());
                return;
            }

            // First check if this is a channel-based characteristic
            ChannelUID channelUID = channelMap.get(characteristic.getUID().toString());
            if (channelUID != null) {
                // This is a channel-based characteristic
                State newState = characteristic.toState(changedEvent.getNewValue().orElse(null));
                if (newState != null) {
                    // Find linked items for this channel
                    linkRegistry.getLinks(channelUID).forEach(link -> {
                        String itemName = link.getItemName();
                        exitEvents.put(itemName, new ExitEvent(newState, event.getMetadata()));
                        eventPublisher.post(ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent(itemName, newState));
                    });
                }
            } else {
                // This is an item-based characteristic
                ItemUID itemUID = itemMap.get(characteristic.getUID().toString());
                if (itemUID != null) {
                    State newState = characteristic.toState(changedEvent.getNewValue().orElse(null));
                    if (newState != null) {
                        exitEvents.put(itemUID.toString(), new ExitEvent(newState, event.getMetadata()));
                        eventPublisher.post(ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent(itemUID.getItemName(), newState));
                    }
                }
            }
        } catch (Exception e) {
            logger.error("{}Failed to handle characteristic event: {}", LOG_PREFIX, e.getMessage());
        }
    }
}
```

```java
/**
 * The {@link HomekitAccessoryBridge} manages the integration between OpenHAB and HomeKit using an accessory-based configuration.
 * It handles the complete lifecycle of HomeKit accessories, including creation, updates, and removal.
 *
 * This class implements {@link EventSubscriber} to handle:
 * - Item state changes for HomeKit-enabled items
 * - {@link HomekitCharacteristic} value updates
 * - {@link HomekitAccessory} registration and cleanup
 *
 * The bridge maintains thread-safe collections for:
 * - Accessories ({@link #accessoryMap})
 * - Characteristics ({@link #characteristicMap})
 * - Item/Channel mappings ({@link #itemMap}, {@link #channelMap})
 *
 * The class integrates with:
 * - {@link HomekitAccessory} for accessory lifecycle management
 * - {@link HomekitCharacteristic} for value conversion and validation
 * - {@link org.openhab.core.items.Item OpenHAB's item system} for state synchronization
 * - {@link org.openhab.core.thing.Channel OpenHAB's channel system} for channel-based characteristics
 * - {@link org.openhab.core.events.EventPublisher OpenHAB's event system} for event propagation
 *
 * @author Karel Goderis - Initial Contribution
 * @since 1.0.0
 */
@Component(service = {HomekitAccessoryBridge.class, EventSubscriber.class}, immediate = true)
@NonNullByDefault
public class HomekitAccessoryBridge implements EventSubscriber {
    // ========== Log Message Prefixes ==========
    private static final String LOG_PREFIX = "Homekit Bridge: ";
    private static final String LOG_INIT = LOG_PREFIX + "Init - ";
    private static final String LOG_STATE = LOG_PREFIX + "State - ";
    private static final String LOG_CONFIG = LOG_PREFIX + "Config - ";
    private static final String LOG_ACCESSORY = LOG_PREFIX + "Accessory - ";
    private static final String LOG_ERROR = LOG_PREFIX + "Error - ";
    private static final String LOG_WARN = LOG_PREFIX + "Warning - ";

    private static final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(HomekitAccessoryBridge.class);
    // ... existing code ...

    /**
     * Handles an item event by converting it to a HomeKit characteristic update.
     *
     * This method processes item events (commands or states) and converts them to HomeKit characteristic
     * updates. It handles both channel-based and item-based characteristics, manages event correlation
     * to prevent loops, and publishes the appropriate events.
     *
     * Key implementation details:
     * - Converts item values to HomeKit characteristic values
     * - Manages exit event correlation to prevent feedback loops
     * - Creates appropriate event metadata
     * - Publishes characteristic update events
     *
     * @param itemName The name of the item being processed
     * @param value The command or state value to be processed
     * @param characteristic The HomeKit characteristic to update
     */
    private void handleItemEvent(String itemName, Object value, HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic) {
        try {
            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
            HomekitCharacteristic<Object> typedCharacteristic = (HomekitCharacteristic<Object>) characteristic;
            JsonValue jsonValue = typedCharacteristic.toValueJson(value);
            if (jsonValue != null) {
                // Check for exit event correlation
                ExitEvent exitEvent = exitEvents.get(itemName);
                if (exitEvent != null && !exitEvent.isExpired()) {
                    logger.debug("{}Using correlated event metadata for item {}", LOG_STATE, itemName);
                    // Use the metadata from the exit event to prevent loops
                    HomekitCharacteristicUpdateEvent updateEvent = new HomekitCharacteristicUpdateEvent(
                        characteristic,
                        null, // old value
                        jsonValue,
                        Collections.emptyMap(),
                        exitEvent.getMetadata()
                    );
                    eventManager.publishEvent(updateEvent);
                    exitEvents.remove(itemName);
                } else {
                    logger.debug("{}Creating new event metadata for item {}", LOG_STATE, itemName);
                    // Create new metadata for uncorrelated event
                    HomekitEventMetadata metadata = new HomekitEventMetadata(
                        (UID) bridgeUID,
                        null,
                        (UID) bridgeUID,
                        peerGroup
                    );
                    HomekitCharacteristicUpdateEvent updateEvent = new HomekitCharacteristicUpdateEvent(
                        characteristic,
                        null, // old value
                        jsonValue,
                        Collections.emptyMap(),
                        metadata
                    );
                    eventManager.publishEvent(updateEvent);
                }
            }
        } catch (Exception e) {
            logger.error("{}Failed to handle event for item {}: {}", LOG_ERROR, itemName, e.getMessage(), e);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Handles item command events from OpenHAB.

     * Key implementation details:
     * - Validates input parameters

     * - Handles both channel and item-based characteristics
     * - Delegates to handleItemEvent for actual processing
     *
     * @param event The item command event to process
     */
    public void handleItemCommand(ItemCommandEvent event) {
        if (event == null || event.getItemName() == null) {
            logger.warn("{}Received null item command event", LOG_WARN);
            return;
        }

        // Clean up expired exit events
        cleanupExpiredExitEvents();

        String itemName = event.getItemName();
        Command command = event.getItemCommand();
        if (command == null) {
            logger.warn("{}Received null command for item {}", LOG_WARN, itemName);
            return;
        }

        logger.debug("{}Processing command for item {}: {}", LOG_STATE, itemName, command);

        // First check if this item is linked to a channel
        ChannelUID channelUID = itemChannelMap.get(itemName);
        if (channelUID != null) {
            // This is a channel-based characteristic
            HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic = channelCharacteristicMap.get(channelUID);
            if (characteristic != null) {
                handleItemEvent(itemName, command, characteristic);
            } else {
                logger.warn("{}No characteristic found for channel {} of item {}", LOG_WARN, channelUID, itemName);
            }
        } else {
            // This is an item-based characteristic
            HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic = characteristicMap.get(itemName);
            if (characteristic != null) {
                handleItemEvent(itemName, command, characteristic);
            } else {
                logger.warn("{}No characteristic found for item {}", LOG_WARN, itemName);
            }
        }
    }

            return;

            return;
```

**User**

Is there a way in opemHAB to directly send events to Things? 

---

**Cursor**

Let me search for information about sending events directly to Things in OpenHAB.


Based on the search results, I can explain how events can be sent to Things in OpenHAB:

1. **Direct Channel Communication**
The primary way to send events to Things is through their channels using the `ThingHandler` interface. This is done by:
- Using `handleCommand(ChannelUID channelUID, Command command)` to send commands
- Using `updateState(ChannelUID channelUID, State state)` to update states

2. **Event Bus Communication**
OpenHAB provides an event bus system that can be used to communicate with Things:
- Things can subscribe to events using `EventSubscriber`
- Events can be published using `EventPublisher`
- The event system supports both commands and state updates

3. **Profile-based Communication**
OpenHAB uses profiles to handle communication between Items and Things:
- Profiles can be created to handle bidirectional communication
- They provide a standardized way to convert between Item and Thing states/commands
- Profiles can be configured with custom logic for state/command conversion

Here's a practical example of how to send events to a Thing:

```java
// Using ThingHandler directly
thingHandler.handleCommand(channelUID, command);
thingHandler.updateState(channelUID, state);

// Using EventPublisher
eventPublisher.post(ChannelEventFactory.createCommandEvent(channelUID, command));
eventPublisher.post(ChannelEventFactory.createStateEvent(channelUID, state));
```

The recommended approach is to:
1. Use `ThingHandler` methods directly when you have a reference to the handler
2. Use the event bus when you need to communicate across components
3. Use profiles when you need standardized conversion between Items and Things

4. **Characteristic-Specific Constraints**:

   - `HomekitCarbonMonoxideLevelCharacteristic`: 0-1000 ppm with 1 ppm step
   - `HomekitTargetHorizontalTiltAngleCharacteristic`: -90 to 90 arcdegrees
   - `HomekitTransmitPowerCharacteristic`: -128 to 127 dBm

7. **Default Values**:
   If configuration parameters are not specified, each characteristic type has sensible defaults:
   - Integer characteristics: minValue = 0, maxValue = Integer.MAX_VALUE
   - Float characteristics: minValue = 0.0, maxValue = 100.0, minStep = 1.0
   - Byte characteristics: minValue = 0, maxValue = Byte.MAX_VALUE

Let me analyze the current implementation and suggest improvements:

1. **Current Implementation**:
   - The base characteristic classes (`HomekitIntegerCharacteristic`, `HomekitFloatCharacteristic`, etc.) have `final` fields for `minValue`, `maxValue`, and other parameters
   - The `HomekitAccessoryBridge` tries to modify these values through reflection using `withMinValue`, `withMaxValue`, and `withStep` methods
   - However, these methods don't exist in the base classes, making the reflection calls ineffective

2. **Issues**:
   - The YAML configuration can't override the characteristic-specific constraints because:
     - The fields are `final`
     - The reflection-based approach doesn't work due to missing methods
     - The values are set in constructors and can't be changed afterward

3. **Suggested Improvements**:

```java
public abstract class HomekitIntegerCharacteristic extends AbstractHomekitCharacteristic<Integer> {
    // Change from final to protected
    protected int minValue;
    protected int maxValue;
    protected String unit;
    
    // Add builder methods
    public HomekitIntegerCharacteristic withMinValue(int minValue) {
        this.minValue = minValue;
        return this;
    }
    
    public HomekitIntegerCharacteristic withMaxValue(int maxValue) {
        this.maxValue = maxValue;
        return this;
    }
    
    public HomekitIntegerCharacteristic withUnit(String unit) {
        this.unit = unit;
        return this;
    }
    
    // Add validation method
    @Override
    public boolean isAllowedValue(Integer value) {
        return value != null && value >= minValue && value <= maxValue;
    }
}
```

4. **Characteristic-Specific Constraints**:
   - Each characteristic should still enforce its own constraints through `isAllowedValue()`
   - For example, `HomekitTargetTemperatureCharacteristic` should still enforce 10-38°C range
   - The YAML configuration should only be able to override within these constraints

5. **Implementation Strategy**:
   a. Remove `final` modifiers from the base characteristic classes
   b. Add builder methods (`withMinValue`, `withMaxValue`, etc.)
   c. Keep characteristic-specific constraints in `isAllowedValue()`
   d. Update the bridge to properly apply YAML configurations

6. **Example Usage**:
```yaml
characteristics:
  targetTemperature:
    item: "openhab:item:Thermostat_Temperature"
    minValue: 15  # Can only be set between 10-38
    maxValue: 30  # Can only be set between 10-38
    step: 0.5     # Can only be set between 0.1-1.0
```

7. **Value Validation**:
```java
public class HomekitTargetTemperatureCharacteristic extends HomekitFloatCharacteristic {
    @Override
    public boolean isAllowedValue(Double value) {
        // First check the base range (10-38)
        if (value == null || value < 10.0 || value > 38.0) {
            return false;
        }
        // Then check if it's within the configured range
        return value >= minValue && value <= maxValue;
    }
}
```

```java
@Override
public void setValue(@Nullable T value) throws Exception {
    if (!isPairedWrite) {
        throw new Exception("Cannot modify a readonly characteristic");
    }
    if (value != null && !isAllowedValue(value)) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Value " + value + " is not allowed for this characteristic");
    }
    @Nullable
    T oldValue = this.value;
    setValueInternal(value);
    notifyValueChanged(oldValue, this.value);
}

@Override
public final void setValue(JsonValue jsonValue) throws Exception {
    if (!isPairedWrite) {
        throw new Exception("Cannot modify a readonly characteristic");
    }
    try {
        T convertedValue = toValue(jsonValue);
        if (convertedValue != null && !isAllowedValue(convertedValue)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Value " + convertedValue + " is not allowed for this characteristic");
        }
        setValue(convertedValue);
    } catch (Exception e) {
        logger.error("{}Error while setting JSON value: {}", LOG_ERROR, e.getMessage(), e);
        throw e;
    }
}

protected void setValue(JsonValue value, Map<String, Object> conversionMap, HomekitEventMetadata metadata)
        throws Exception {
    if (!isPairedWrite) {
        throw new Exception("Cannot modify a readonly characteristic");
    }
    try {
        T convertedValue = toValue(value, conversionMap);
        if (convertedValue != null && !isAllowedValue(convertedValue)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Value " + convertedValue + " is not allowed for this characteristic");
        }
        @Nullable
        T oldValue = this.value;
        setValueInternal(convertedValue);
        notifyValueChanged(oldValue, this.value, metadata);
    } catch (Exception e) {
        logger.error("{}Error while setting value with metadata: {}", LOG_ERROR, e.getMessage(), e);
        throw e;
    }
}
```

3. **Error Handling**: Provides clear error messages when invalid values are attempted
4. **Consistency**: Validates values consistently across all setValue methods
5. **Documentation**: Makes it clear to implementers that they should override `isAllowedValue` to provide proper validation

- `HomekitTargetTemperatureCharacteristic` (10-38°C)
- `HomekitServiceLabelIndexCharacteristic` (1-255)
- `HomekitTransmitPowerCharacteristic` (-128 to 127 dBm)

```java
/**
 * Loads all accessory configurations from the configuration manager.
 *
 * <p>
 * This method loads and processes all accessory configurations:
 * <ul>
 *   <li>Retrieves all configurations from {@link HomekitConfigurationManager}</li>
 *   <li>Processes each accessory configuration by UID</li>
 *   <li>Creates new accessories or updates existing ones</li>
 *   <li>Removes accessories that are no longer in any configuration</li>
 * </ul>
 * </p>
 */
private void loadConfiguration() {
    // Load all accessory configurations from YAML
    Map<String, Map<String, Object>> allConfigs = configManager.getAllConfigurations(
            HomekitConfigurationManager.ConfigurationType.ACCESSORY);
    
    if (allConfigs.isEmpty()) {
        logger.warn("{}No accessory configurations found", LOG_PREFIX);
        return;
    }

    // Keep track of configured UIDs to identify orphaned accessories
    Set<String> configuredUids = new HashSet<>();

    // Process each configuration by UID
    allConfigs.forEach((uid, config) -> {
        try {
            configuredUids.add(uid);
            
            // Get the accessories map from the configuration
            @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
            Map<String, Object> accessories = (Map<String, Object>) config.get("accessories");
            if (accessories == null) {
                logger.warn("{}No accessories found in configuration for UID {}", LOG_PREFIX, uid);
                return;
            }

            // Process each accessory in the configuration
            accessories.forEach((accessoryUid, accessoryConfig) -> {
                try {
                    if (accessoryMap.containsKey(accessoryUid)) {
                        updateAccessory(accessoryUid, (Map<String, Object>) accessoryConfig);
                    } else {
                        createAccessory(accessoryUid, (Map<String, Object>) accessoryConfig);
                    }
                } catch (Exception e) {
                    logger.error("{}Failed to process accessory {} in configuration {}: {}", 
                        LOG_PREFIX, accessoryUid, uid, e.getMessage());
                }
            });
        } catch (Exception e) {
            logger.error("{}Failed to process configuration for UID {}: {}", 
                LOG_PREFIX, uid, e.getMessage());
        }
    });

    // Remove accessories that are no longer in any configuration
    Set<String> orphanedUids = new HashSet<>(accessoryMap.keySet());
    orphanedUids.removeAll(configuredUids);
    orphanedUids.forEach(this::removeAccessory);
```
```java
}
```

Looking at the codebase, I can see that this pattern is used in several places, particularly in the `HomekitAccessoryBridge` and `HomekitThingBridge` classes. The ThingHandler is responsible for:

1. Managing the channel's state
2. Handling commands sent to the channel
3. Updating the channel's state
4. Managing the lifecycle of the channel

The ThingHandler is obtained through the Thing's `getHandler()` method, which is part of OpenHAB's core Thing API. This handler is responsible for all interactions with the channel and its underlying device or service.

In the HomeKit binding specifically, the handlers are created by the `HomekitHandlerFactory` and can be either:

3. **Configuration**:
The bridge supports both types through configuration:
```java
private void applyCharacteristicConfig(HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic, Map<String, Object> config) {
    // Handle item/channel mapping
    String itemName = (String) config.get("item");
    String channelId = (String) config.get("channel");
    if (itemName != null) {
        itemMap.put(characteristic.getUID().toString(), new ItemUID(itemName));
    }
    if (channelId != null) {

    }
}
```

So to answer your question: No, the HomekitAccessoryBridge does not only support channels that are linked to items. It supports:

1. **Direct Item Mapping**: Characteristics can be directly mapped to items without going through channels
2. **Channel-based Mapping**: Characteristics can be mapped to channels, which may or may not be linked to items
3. **Hybrid Approach**: Some characteristics can use channels while others use direct item mapping

The bridge is designed to be flexible and support both approaches, allowing for:
- Direct item-to-characteristic mapping for simpler cases
- Channel-based mapping for more complex scenarios where you need the additional features of channels (like profiles, state conversion, etc.)
- A mix of both approaches depending on the use case

This flexibility is particularly useful when:
- You want to expose simple items directly to HomeKit
- You need the additional features of channels (like profiles for state conversion)
- You're working with existing Things that already have channel configurations
- You want to maintain backward compatibility with different configuration styles

**Cursor**

Let me analyze how the HomekitAccessoryBridge handles sending events from Characteristics to Channels:


Yes, you're correct. Looking at the code, particularly in the `handleCharacteristicEvent` method of `HomekitAccessoryBridge`, we can see that events from Characteristics to Channels are only sent if the Channel is linked to an Item:

```java
// First check if this is a channel-based characteristic
ChannelUID channelUID = channelMap.get(characteristic.getUID().toString());
if (channelUID != null) {
    // This is a channel-based characteristic
    State newState = characteristic.toState(changedEvent.getNewValue().orElse(null));
    if (newState != null) {
        // Find linked items for this channel
        linkRegistry.getLinks(channelUID).forEach(link -> {
            String itemName = link.getItemName();
            exitEvents.put(itemName, new ExitEvent(newState, event.getMetadata()));
            eventPublisher.post(ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent(itemName, newState));
        });
    }
}
```

The key points are:

1. When a characteristic value changes, the bridge:
   - First checks if it's a channel-based characteristic
   - If it is, it converts the new value to a State
   - Then it looks for linked items using `linkRegistry.getLinks(channelUID)`
   - Only if there are linked items, it sends state events to those items

2. There's no direct way to send events to unlinked channels because:
   - The OpenHAB event system is designed around Items
   - State changes are propagated through Items
   - Channels without linked Items don't have a way to receive state updates

3. This means that:
   - Characteristics can be mapped to channels
   - But state updates from those characteristics will only be propagated if the channel is linked to an item
   - Unlinked channels won't receive state updates from their characteristics

This is a limitation of the OpenHAB architecture, where:
- Items are the primary state holders
- Channels are conduits between Things and Items
- State changes must flow through Items to be properly tracked and managed

If you need to handle state changes for unlinked channels, you would need to:
1. Either link them to Items (even if those Items are just for internal use)
2. Or implement a different mechanism for state management that doesn't rely on the OpenHAB event system

```java

            exitEvents.put(itemName, new ExitEvent(newState, event.getMetadata()));
            eventPublisher.post(ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent(itemName, newState));
        });
    }
}
```

**Cursor**

Let me analyze this question carefully by looking at how ThingHandlers and channels are typically used in OpenHAB:


After analyzing the code, I would say that it's generally not recommended to deviate from the OpenHAB best practices by sending events directly to unlinked Thing Channels. Here's why:

1. **OpenHAB's Architecture Design**:
   - OpenHAB is designed with Items as the primary state holders
   - Channels are meant to be conduits between Things and Items
   - The event system is built around Items, not Channels

2. **Potential Issues with Direct Channel Updates**:
   - State tracking might be inconsistent
   - Event correlation could break
   - Profiles won't be applied
   - State persistence might not work correctly
   - Other bindings or rules might not receive updates

3. **Better Alternatives**:
   Instead of directly updating unlinked channels, consider:
   ```java
   // Option 1: Create internal Items for state tracking
   private void createInternalItem(ChannelUID channelUID) {
       String itemName = "internal_" + channelUID.toString();
       // Create and link the item
       // Then use normal event flow
   }

   // Option 2: Use ThingHandler's updateState
   private void updateChannelState(ChannelUID channelUID, State state) {
       Thing thing = thingRegistry.get(channelUID.getThingUID());
       if (thing != null) {
           ThingHandler handler = thing.getHandler();
           if (handler != null) {
               handler.updateState(channelUID, state);
           }
       }
   }
   ```

4. **If You Must Deviate**:
   If you absolutely need to update unlinked channels, at least:
   - Document why you're deviating from the standard pattern
   - Implement proper state tracking
   - Handle error cases
   - Consider the impact on other parts of the system
   - Make it clear in the code that this is a deviation

5. **Long-term Considerations**:
   - Future OpenHAB versions might change how channels work
   - Other bindings might expect the standard pattern
   - Debugging could be more difficult
   - State persistence might not work as expected

The recommended approach would be to:
1. Create internal Items for state tracking if needed
2. Use the standard event flow through Items
3. If that's not possible, use the ThingHandler's `updateState` method
4. Document any deviations from the standard pattern

This maintains compatibility with OpenHAB's architecture while still allowing you to achieve your goals.

```java
    Channel channel = thing.getChannel(channelUID);
    if (channel != null) {
```

2. **Using Channel Link Events**:
```java
@Override
public void channelLinked(ChannelUID channelUID) {
    // Called when a channel is linked to an item
    Channel channel = thing.getChannel(channelUID);
    if (channel != null) {
        HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic = characteristicMap.get(channel);
        if (characteristic != null) {
            // Subscribe to characteristic events
            eventSubscriptions.add(eventManager.subscribe(
                HomekitEventType.CHARACTERISTIC_VALUE_CHANGED,
                characteristic.getUID(),
                thing.getUID(),
                event -> onCharacteristicEvent((HomekitCharacteristicEvent) event)
            ));
            
            // Update initial state
            Object value = characteristic.getValue();
            if (value instanceof State state) {
                updateState(channelUID, state);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

3. **Using Profiles for Bidirectional Communication**:
```java
private void createProfileForChannel(Channel channel, ItemChannelLink link) {
    // Create OpenHAB -> HomeKit profile
    Profile openhabToHomekitProfile = profileFactory.createProfile(profileTypeUID, 
        new ProfileCallback() {
            @Override
            public void handleCommand(Command command) {
                handleProfileCommand(channel.getUID(), command);
            }

            @Override
            public void sendUpdate(State state) {
                handleProfileState(channel.getUID(), state);
            }
        }, context);

    // Create HomeKit -> OpenHAB profile
    Profile homekitToOpenhabProfile = profileFactory.createProfile(profileTypeUID,
        new ProfileCallbackImpl(eventPublisher, safeCaller, itemStateConverter, link, 
            thingRegistry::get, this::getItem, this::toAcceptedCommand),
        context);

    // Store both profiles
    channelProfiles.put(channel.getUID(), openhabToHomekitProfile);
    channelHomekitToOpenhabProfiles.put(channel.getUID(), homekitToOpenhabProfile);
}
```

4. **Using Event Subscriptions**:

```java
    eventSubscriptions.add(eventManager.subscribe(
        HomekitEventType.CHARACTERISTIC_VALUE_CHANGED,
        characteristic.getUID(),
        thing.getUID(),
        event -> handleCharacteristicEvent(characteristic, event)
    ));
}
```

The recommended approach depends on your specific use case:

1. For direct channel commands: Use `handleCommand` in your ThingHandler
2. For state updates: Use `updateState` in your ThingHandler
3. For bidirectional communication: Use Profiles
4. For event-based communication: Use Event Subscriptions

The most robust approach would be to combine these methods:

```java
public class YourThingHandler extends BaseThingHandler {
    @Override
    public void handleCommand(ChannelUID channelUID, Command command) {
        // Handle incoming commands
        Channel channel = thing.getChannel(channelUID);
        if (channel != null) {
            HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic = characteristicMap.get(channel);
            if (characteristic != null) {
                handleCharacteristicCommand(characteristic, command);
            }
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void channelLinked(ChannelUID channelUID) {
        // Set up event subscriptions when channel is linked
        Channel channel = thing.getChannel(channelUID);
        if (channel != null) {
            HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic = characteristicMap.get(channel);
            if (characteristic != null) {
                subscribeToCharacteristicEvents(characteristic);
                updateInitialState(channelUID, characteristic);
            }
        }
    }

    private void subscribeToCharacteristicEvents(HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic) {
        eventSubscriptions.add(eventManager.subscribe(
            HomekitEventType.CHARACTERISTIC_VALUE_CHANGED,
            characteristic.getUID(),
            thing.getUID(),
            event -> handleCharacteristicEvent(characteristic, event)
        ));
    }

    private void handleCharacteristicEvent(HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic, HomekitEvent event) {
        if (event instanceof HomekitCharacteristicChangedEvent changedEvent) {
            State newState = characteristic.toState(changedEvent.getNewValue().orElse(null));
            if (newState != null) {
                updateState(getChannelUID(characteristic), newState);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

This approach provides:
- Direct command handling
- Event-based state updates
- Proper channel linking/unlinking
- Bidirectional communication through profiles
- Error handling and logging
- State persistence

```java
}
```

```java
public class ChannelStateListener {
    private final ThingRegistry thingRegistry;
    private final Map<ChannelUID, Consumer<State>> stateListeners = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    public void addListener(ChannelUID channelUID, Consumer<State> listener) {
        stateListeners.put(channelUID, listener);

        Thing thing = thingRegistry.get(channelUID.getThingUID());
        if (thing != null) {
            ThingHandler handler = thing.getHandler();
            if (handler != null) {

                    }
                });
            }
        }
    }

    public void removeListener(ChannelUID channelUID) {
        stateListeners.remove(channelUID);
        Thing thing = thingRegistry.get(channelUID.getThingUID());
        if (thing != null) {

            if (handler != null) {
                handler.removeChannelListener(channelUID);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The recommended approach depends on your specific use case:

1. If you're implementing a ThingHandler:
   - Use the built-in channel listener mechanism
   - Register listeners in initialize()
   - Clean up in dispose()

2. If you're implementing a service that needs to monitor multiple things:
   - Use the EventSubscriber interface
   - Subscribe to relevant event types
   - Handle events in receive()

3. If you need to monitor specific channels:
   - Use EventPublisher to subscribe to specific channels
   - Manage subscriptions manually
   - Clean up in deactivate()

4. If you need a reusable component:
   - Create a custom ChannelStateListener
   - Allow adding/removing listeners
   - Handle cleanup properly

Remember to:
- Always clean up subscriptions and listeners
- Handle errors gracefully
- Consider thread safety
- Log important state changes
- Handle null cases and edge conditions

The most robust approach would be to combine these methods:

```java
@Component(service = { EventSubscriber.class, ThingRegistryChangeListener.class })
public class YourChannelManager implements EventSubscriber, ThingRegistryChangeListener {
    private final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(YourChannelManager.class);
    private final Map<ChannelUID, State> channelStates = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Set<ChannelUID> monitoredChannels = new HashSet<>();

    @Override
    public Set<String> getSubscribedEventTypes() {
        return Set.of(
            "org.openhab.core.thing.events.ThingStatusInfoChangedEvent",
            "org.openhab.core.thing.events.ThingUpdatedEvent"
        );
    }

    @Override
    public void receive(Event event) {
        if (event instanceof ThingUpdatedEvent thingEvent) {
            handleThingUpdate(thingEvent.getThing());
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void thingUpdated(Thing thing) {
        handleThingUpdate(thing);
    }

    private void handleThingUpdate(Thing thing) {
        thing.getChannels().forEach(channel -> {
            ChannelUID channelUID = channel.getUID();
            if (monitoredChannels.contains(channelUID)) {
                // Get the current state from the thing's handler
                ThingHandler handler = thing.getHandler();
                if (handler != null) {
                    State currentState = handler.getState(channelUID);
                    if (currentState != null) {
                        updateChannelState(channelUID, currentState);
                    }
                }
            }
        });
    }

    public void monitorChannel(ChannelUID channelUID) {
        monitoredChannels.add(channelUID);
        // Get initial state
        Thing thing = thingRegistry.get(channelUID.getThingUID());
        if (thing != null) {
            ThingHandler handler = thing.getHandler();
            if (handler != null) {
                State currentState = handler.getState(channelUID);
                if (currentState != null) {
                    updateChannelState(channelUID, currentState);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    public void unmonitorChannel(ChannelUID channelUID) {
        monitoredChannels.remove(channelUID);
        channelStates.remove(channelUID);
    }

    private void updateChannelState(ChannelUID channelUID, State state) {
        channelStates.put(channelUID, state);
        logger.debug("Channel {} state updated to {}", channelUID, state);
        // Your custom logic here
    }

    public State getChannelState(ChannelUID channelUID) {
        return channelStates.get(channelUID);
    }
}
```

```java:src/main/java/org/openhab/io/homekit/bridge/HomekitAccessoryBridge.java
private void handleCharacteristicEvent(HomekitCharacteristic<?> characteristic, HomekitEvent event) {
    if (event instanceof HomekitCharacteristicChangedEvent changedEvent) {
        try {
            // Check if event is from peer group
            if (event.getMetadata().isFromPeerGroup(peerGroup)) {
                logger.debug("{}Ignoring event from peer group: {}", LOG_PREFIX,
                        event.getMetadata().getImmediateOrigin());
                return;
            }

            // First check if this is a channel-based characteristic
            ChannelUID channelUID = channelMap.get(characteristic.getUID().toString());
            if (channelUID != null) {
                // This is a channel-based characteristic
                State newState = characteristic.toState(changedEvent.getNewValue().orElse(null));
                if (newState != null) {
                    // Get linked items for this channel
                    Set<String> linkedItems = linkRegistry.getLinkedItems(channelUID);
                    for (String itemName : linkedItems) {
                        exitEvents.put(itemName, new ExitEvent(newState, event.getMetadata()));
                        eventPublisher.post(ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent(itemName, newState));
                    }
                }
            } else {
                // This is an item-based characteristic
                ItemUID itemUID = itemMap.get(characteristic.getUID().toString());
                if (itemUID != null) {
                    State newState = characteristic.toState(changedEvent.getNewValue().orElse(null));
                    if (newState != null) {
                        exitEvents.put(itemUID.toString(), new ExitEvent(newState, event.getMetadata()));
                        eventPublisher.post(ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent(itemUID.getItemName(), newState));
                    }
                }
            }
        } catch (Exception e) {
            logger.error("{}Failed to handle characteristic event: {}", LOG_PREFIX, e.getMessage());
        }
    }
}
```

  - Participate in rules and scripts
  - Be accessible through the REST API

- Items are managed by OpenHAB's `ItemRegistry`
- The HomeKit bridge only reads the Items, it doesn't create or manage them
- Item creation/deletion is handled by:
  - The OpenHAB configuration system
  - The UI
  - Other bindings
  - User-defined rules

- More direct access to Item objects
- Better type safety (working with `Item` objects instead of just names)
- Access to Item metadata and properties
- Consistent with OpenHAB's architecture
- No need for additional Item tracking

  - Items are deleted
  - Items are modified

Let me show you how `createInternalItem` could be implemented in the `HomekitAccessoryBridge` class:

```java
/**
 * Creates an internal item for tracking unbound channel states.
 * 
 * @param channelUID The channel UID to create an internal item for
 * @return The created internal item
 */
private Item createInternalItem(ChannelUID channelUID) {
    String itemName = "internal_" + channelUID.toString().replace(":", "_");
    
    try {
        // Check if item already exists
        Item existingItem = itemRegistry.get(itemName);
        if (existingItem != null) {
            return existingItem;
        }

        // Determine item type based on channel type
        String itemType = determineItemType(channelUID);
        
        // Create the item
        Item item = itemFactory.createItem(itemType, itemName);
        if (item == null) {
            logger.error("{}Failed to create internal item {} of type {}", 
                LOG_PREFIX, itemName, itemType);
            return null;
        }

        // Add the item to the registry
        itemRegistry.add(item);
        
        // Create the channel link
        ItemChannelLink link = new ItemChannelLink(itemName, channelUID);
        linkRegistry.add(link);
        
        logger.debug("{}Created internal item {} for channel {}", 
            LOG_PREFIX, itemName, channelUID);
            
        return item;
    } catch (Exception e) {
        logger.error("{}Failed to create internal item for channel {}: {}", 
            LOG_PREFIX, channelUID, e.getMessage());
        return null;
    }
}

/**
 * Determines the appropriate item type for a channel.
 * 
 * @param channelUID The channel UID
 * @return The appropriate item type
 */
private String determineItemType(ChannelUID channelUID) {
    // Get the channel type from the thing
    Thing thing = thingRegistry.get(channelUID.getThingUID());
    if (thing != null) {
        Channel channel = thing.getChannel(channelUID.getId());
        if (channel != null) {
            ChannelType channelType = channelTypeRegistry.getChannelType(channel.getChannelTypeUID());
            if (channelType != null) {
                // Map channel type to item type
                return mapChannelTypeToItemType(channelType);
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Default to Switch if we can't determine the type
    return "Switch";
}

/**
 * Maps a channel type to an appropriate item type.
 * 
 * @param channelType The channel type
 * @return The appropriate item type
 */
private String mapChannelTypeToItemType(ChannelType channelType) {
    // This would need to be implemented based on your channel type to item type mapping
    // For example:
    switch (channelType.getKind()) {
        case STATE:
            if (channelType.getState().getPattern() != null) {
                return "String";
            }
            return "Switch";
        case TRIGGER:
            return "String";
        default:
            return "Switch";
    }
}
```

Ah, now I understand your point better! Let me clarify:

You're absolutely right. If we're sending events to Items, we don't need profile transformations because:

1. **Item Events are the Source of Truth**:
   - Items are the primary state holders in OpenHAB
   - When an Item's state changes, it's already in the correct format
   - The Profile is only needed when going from Channel to Item or vice versa

2. **Current Implementation**:
```java

State newState = characteristic.toState(changedEvent.getNewValue().orElse(null));
if (newState != null) {
    String itemName = itemChannelLinkRegistry.getLinks(channelUID).stream().findFirst()
            .map(ItemChannelLink::getItemName).orElse(null);
    if (itemName != null) {
        exitEvents.put(itemName, new ExitEvent(newState, event.getMetadata()));
        eventPublisher.post(ItemEventFactory.createStateEvent(itemName, newState));
    }
}
```
This is actually correct! Because:
- We're sending the state directly to the Item
- The Item will then trigger its own state change event
- That event will be picked up by `handleItemState`
- No profile transformation is needed at this point

3. **The Flow Should Be**:
```
HomeKit -> Characteristic -> Item (direct state update)
Item -> ItemStateEvent -> handleItemState -> Characteristic -> HomeKit
```

So I was wrong in my previous response. The current implementation is actually following the correct pattern:
1. When HomeKit changes a characteristic, we update the Item state directly
2. When the Item state changes, we listen for that event and update HomeKit
3. No profile transformation is needed because we're working with Item states directly

The Profiles would only be needed if we were:
1. Going directly from Channel to ThingHandler
2. Or if we needed to transform the state format between Channel and Item
